answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying each identity to a costly, verifiable track record rather than a free signup. Like a trellis that only supports vines that have actually grown along it, an agent earns trust gradually through completed work, staked collateral, and endorsements from established peers. A newcomer called raven cannot simply clone itself a thousand times, because each copy starts with zero history and zero stake. Any fake reputation needs real resources, and the ripple of one exposed fraud — slashed stake and revoked endorsements — makes mass forgery unprofitable.
